clue.text: Completely black geysers do

parts.note: up means completely, as in 'eaten up' or 'used up'
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Geysers are imagined spouting something entirely black.
explanation.walkthrough: UPJET is a rare verb in Chambers, to spout upward. 'Completely black' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser throws its water skyward, which is exactly what this verb of upward spouting describes.

clue.text: Din maybe with head moving to end silence? The opposite

indicators.note: the first letter travels round to finish the word

parts.note: Gunga Din, Kipling's water-carrier, so Din is one example of a Gunga

explanation.surface: A noise that rises to drown out the quiet, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Din' looks like noise, the opposite of silence, but it is Kipling's Gunga Din.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to silence, so freeing someone's mouth to speak is the reverse of silencing.

clue.text: Soft on e.g. sailor, sexy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
a sailor is a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A soft spot for sailors, who are deemed sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor is not a seaman but a straw hat with a flat brim.
explanation.definitionFit: Phat is slang praise for anything excellent, and especially for an attractive, sexy person.

clue.text: Gemstone creating quarrel with thug

parts.note: a jar is a quarrel or clash
a goon is a hired thug

explanation.surface: A precious stone sparks a fight with a heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargoon is a colourless or pale variety of zircon cut as a gem.

clue.text: English term of affection (not accepted) for old-fashioned 'breeding'

parts.note: ENG is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: not means without, so the following item is taken out

parts.note: an endearment is a pet name
A is the abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: An English pet name, now out of favour, for upbringing in old-fashioned terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' marks the answer as obsolete; the quoted 'breeding' means begetting, not good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Engenderment is an obsolete noun for engendering, the act of begetting or producing offspring.

clue.text: Crumpet turned up with bread, Indian originally

indicators.note: turned round, the following short word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
naan is leavened Indian flatbread

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A crumpet turned over with naan, an Indian twist on teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumpet turned up' looks like a toasted teacake flipped; crumpet is British slang for women seen as sexual objects, and 'up' is the word turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are vulgar slang: crumpet for women viewed sexually, and this word for a woman's genitals or women collectively.

clue.text: Get drunk old fool going too far?

parts.note: an ass is a fool
OTT, over the top, means going too far

explanation.surface: A daft old man has had far too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSOTT is a Spenserian word, to besot or infatuate; 'Get drunk' is read as 'make sottish', i.e. besot.
explanation.definitionFit: The obsolete verb means to besot, to make someone stupefied as if by drink.

clue.text: Opposition sat in groups untidily

indicators.note: arranged into groups in a messy way, these letters are regrouped

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Protesters staged a messy sit-in in clusters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat in' evokes a sit-in protest by the opposition; read 'groups untidily' as a verb phrase, the setter shuffling the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antis are people opposed to something, collectively the opposition.

clue.text: Skipper e.g. holding sport up

indicators.note: holding means having something inside

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A team captain, perhaps, keeps the sport going.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipper looks like a captain; it is a name for this fish, which skims the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The saury is a long-beaked fish also known as the skipper because it leaps along the water.

clue.text: One can't be doing with rogues hiding dad's trainers

definitions.text: One can't be doing with rogues

indicators.note: a hiding is a thrashing, so these letters are beaten into new shape

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man who cannot stand villains stashing his father's sports shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' reads as concealing; it is a beating. Rogues here are items that stray from the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is an untypical specimen, and someone imposing uniformity has no patience for anything that deviates.

clue.text: We're prickly when caught in bad weather, climbing

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it
climbing in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: sleet is wet, unpleasant weather
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Plants complain they become spiky when trapped in foul weather while growing upward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the plural first person: the answer describes itself. Only the weather word climbs; the word for 'when' then sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasels are plants with spiny stems and bristly flower heads, so they are prickly.

clue.text: Barman, one trying to limit reduced pressure

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it on both sides

parts.note: a taster tries food or drink
pressure cut down to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A barman tries to keep pressure down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws beer from the tap, an old word for a barman.

clue.text: Ostrich to let go, head to tail

indicators.note: the leading letter is moved round to the back of the word

parts.note: to unhand someone is to release them

explanation.surface: An instruction for releasing an ostrich, pulling it head to tail.
explanation.walkthrough: NHANDU (or nandu) is the rhea, the South American bird often called the American ostrich.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless bird closely resembling an ostrich, and is so called in Chambers.

clue.text: Strangeness in e.g. Congo making one bewildered (5, two words)

indicators.note: one item sits inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: Congo (congou) is a kind of black China tea, so it is 'a tea'
S is the physicist's symbol for strangeness, a quantum number

explanation.surface: Something odd about the Congo leaves a traveller confused.
explanation.walkthrough: Congo is not the country but a grade of tea. The '(5, two words)' is the printed enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is the idiom for being confused and lost.

clue.text: Prodigious timber tree protected by grand Malay lord

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded by its guardians, so one part sits within the others

parts.note: G is short for grand
the argan is a Moroccan tree with hard wood
tuan is a Malay title, sir or lord

explanation.surface: A huge tree is guarded by a Malay aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantuan, from Rabelais's giant, is a synonym of enormous or prodigious.

clue.text: Equity is safer when spread — number invested

indicators.note: invested means wrapped or placed within, so one letter goes inside
something spread out is scattered, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Investment advice: shares are safer spread around with a number of holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equity' and 'invested' make it read like finance; equity here is justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity in its legal and moral sense is fairness, even-handed justice.

clue.text: Heavies discourse at length, reverse of gloomy

parts.note: to go on is to talk at length

indicators.note: the word for gloomy is to be read from back to front

parts.note: sad means gloomy

explanation.surface: Heavy types droning on are the opposite of downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A goonda is an Indian word for a hired thug or ruffian.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavies are hired strong-arm men, which is what goondas are in Indian English.

clue.text: Conference turning in recondite ideas

indicators.note: turning round means the run of letters reads backwards
the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: At a conference, obscure ideas start to change course.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative or deliberative assembly, i.e. a formal conference.

clue.text: Time to relax after close of day for 'mountain man'

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: eve is evening, the close of day
rest is time to relax

explanation.surface: A mountaineer gets some downtime at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close of day' suggests the letter Y, but it is the evening itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Everest was the surveyor whose surname was given to the world's highest peak, so he is the mountain's man.

clue.text: One in the transfer market, Blackburn player gets hold of them?

indicators.note: getting hold of something means having it within one's grip

parts.note: Blackburn Rovers is an English football club
'em is short for them

explanation.surface: A Blackburn footballer active in the transfer window signs players.
explanation.walkthrough: The football frame misleads: the transfer here is of furniture, by a removal firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A remover works for a removals firm, moving people's belongings between houses for a fee.

clue.text: Prepare to rock? No more, dancer dancing central bit of veleta

indicators.note: letters that dance move about and settle in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: only the middle of the following word is kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six

explanation.surface: Bracing for some rock music? Not any more: the dancer is busy with an old-time veleta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' marks the answer as obsolete (Spenserian). A veleta is an old-time British ballroom dance in waltz time; 'rock' is to rock a baby, not rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: To encradle is to lay a baby in its cradle, ready to be rocked to sleep.

clue.text: Apprehend what's appropriate in remedial treatment

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: a cure is a course of remedial treatment
apt means appropriate

explanation.surface: Grasp what's suitable in therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend a suspect is to arrest or seize them.

clue.text: Fido's escaped, dammit

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a pet dog
has escaped means has gone

explanation.surface: An owner's curse on finding the dog has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'has', so 'Fido's escaped' is the dog has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is an American euphemistic oath, a milder way of saying damned.

clue.text: Jumping event — amateur entering entered blind

indicators.note: letters that jump about land in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: having entered, one is in
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: At a show-jumping event an amateur rider entered without being able to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping event' reads as show jumping, but the jumping is done by the letters of 'event'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian is a window blind of horizontal slats, short for Venetian blind.

clue.text: Ruler in eastern commune

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a mir was a Russian peasant village commune

explanation.surface: A ruler living in a commune somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or governor, a ruler of an emirate.

clue.text: Sowar missing conflict? Yep, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the letters
missing means lacking, so the word that follows is taken out

parts.note: a sowar is an Indian cavalry trooper
the letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked if an Indian trooper missed the war, someone answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus WAR is an anagram of SOWAR plus YEP. As a whole the clue describes an Indian soldier who, unlike a sowar, is not a cavalryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepoy was an Indian infantry soldier in British service, a close cousin of the cavalry sowar.

clue.text: Special block of paper with German titling possibly

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
a pad is a block of writing paper
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A special notepad on which titles are written in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titling' is not putting titles on things but a bird: the hedge sparrow or meadow pipit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spadger is dialect for a sparrow, and the titling (hedge sparrow) is one example, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Sacks upended as form of lure

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means turned bottom to top

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: Bags turned upside down to make a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacks' looks like bags but is the verb, plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a decoy, a perch for a tethered bird used to lure others, as in stool pigeon.

clue.text: As was serene in torpor or idleness

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the words that follow, across their gaps

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone was calm while lounging in sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serene' is not calm here: as an obsolete noun it meant the light dew of evening (French serein).
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an old adjective for dewy, describing what the evening serene was like.

clue.text: Pullman compartment redirected to end of the Metro

indicators.note: something sent a different way is rerouted, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the last letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Pullman sleeper carriage section is diverted to the terminus of the underground.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pullman is a luxury railway carriage; the answer is American railroad usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomette is a small single-berth private sleeping compartment in a US railway carriage.

clue.text: Pox is confusing by the sound of it

indicators.note: we go on how the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to pie type is to jumble it, so pies means mixes up

explanation.surface: Smallpox is confusing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old mild oath, as in 'a pize on him', used like 'a pox on him'.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word was used in curses exactly as pox was, so it stands for a pox.

clue.text: Foreground figure European artist drops in, flanked by his king and queen

indicators.note: things flanked by others have them on either side

parts.note: the artist is French, so his king is a roi
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so those letters are lost

parts.note: Nicolas Poussin, the 17th-century French painter
the letters the painter drops
R for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A European painter pops in, escorted by his king and queen, as a figure in the foreground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops in' looks like 'visits', but the painter loses the letters IN. 'His' tells you to put his king into French; the French painter's name is short for the one chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A repoussoir is a figure or object placed in a painting's foreground to push the eye back into depth.

clue.text: Sign in bars, 'Good having singles around'? The reverse

indicators.note: the result of the quoted instruction is turned backwards
something placed around another encloses it, putting it inside

parts.note: singles are ones
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sign in a pub says 'Good, having single measures around' and then its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The bars are musical bars, not pubs: segno is the sign marking where a repeat begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Segno, Italian for sign, is the notation marking the start or end of a repeated passage in music.

clue.text: Opera the French love on being denied heaven!

parts.note: love is nothing, and the French for nothing is rien

indicators.note: what is denied is refused, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Zion is heaven, the holy city
the letters removed

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an opera's French love goes on without heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so 'the French love' is French for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rienzi is Wagner's early grand opera about the Roman tribune Cola di Rienzi.

clue.text: After end of parliament, tyro bungled line for explosive

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: its final letter

indicators.note: something bungled is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: When parliament breaks up, a novice fluffs the wiring for a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotyl is another name for trinitrotoluene, the high explosive TNT.

clue.text: Church about right, one responsible for leader showing faith

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
R is the abbreviation for right
an editor writes the leader, the paper's main opinion column

explanation.surface: A churchman about to turn right as head of the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a church head, but it is a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a system of religious belief, i.e. a faith.
